subject: physics

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2020 (Q6) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the angle of contact θ is the angle between the tangent to the liquid surface at the point of contact and the tangent to the solid surface, measured INSIDE the liquid. θ is acute when the adhesive force between liquid and solid exceeds the cohesive force within the liquid, and the liquid wets the solid (water on clean glass, θ near 8°); θ is obtuse when cohesion dominates and the liquid does not wet the solid (mercury on glass, θ near 140°). Angle values corrected 2026-09-03: the question asks for PURE water, whose angle of contact on clean glass is about 0°, not the roughly 8° an ordinary water sample on ordinary glass gives; both are now stated. The Sri Chaitanya 2026-27 physics volume prints 0° for pure water and 140° for mercury (VSAQ 18, printed p.107).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. The words measured inside the liquid are part of the definition, not an extra.
steps.why: The same picture offers two angles that add to 180°. The words inside the liquid are what pick one of them, so the definition is incomplete without them.
common_mistakes: Leaving out measured inside the liquid, which leaves the supplementary angle equally valid.
Saying the angle is between the solid surface and the vertical. It is between the solid surface and the tangent to the liquid surface.

lines.text: Acute θ: wets · Obtuse θ: does not wet

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give one acute example and one obtuse example by name.
steps.why: The value of θ is set by the size of adhesion against cohesion, so naming both forces is what makes the acute and obtuse cases follow instead of being memorised.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two cases. Water on glass is acute, mercury on glass is obtuse.
Using cohesion for the liquid–solid force. Adhesion is between the liquid and the solid; cohesion is within the liquid.

recall.must_convey: That θ is acute when adhesion is larger and the liquid wets the solid, and obtuse when cohesion is larger and it does not.
accept: water on glass wets, mercury does not

steps.memory_tip: Water on glass is acute and wetting. Mercury on glass is obtuse and not wetting.

insider_note: The phrase measured inside the liquid carries the first mark; the second needs a named pair, water on glass against mercury on glass.
